Guarded by contract_invariants.rs::the_elements_schema_pins_the_version_and_rule_the_code_emits and walked against every fixture's artifact by draft_schemas.rs.
title: ethos.parser.elements.v0
description: A document's items, one flat list, each with its page, its box, its text, the representation nodes it covers and a label the record states. A PROJECTION of the representation, not the record: it reads no rule of its own about what a piece of text is. A text unit is a block of the reading-order cut (the element ethos.grounding.v1 cites), consecutive blocks sharing a page and a layout_unit joined into one, and a DOCX paragraph's runs one unit (decision #130); a label is a run's page furniture, a Word header's or footer's included, else a heading level a DOCX, ODF or EPUB file declares, else its tagged role path after the document's RoleMap read innermost first, else its inferred heading at levels 1-6, else `text`; a table is every table record, with its box where the record measured one; a picture is a painted image placement or a measured figure region, with the text of each unit holding a run the record names inside it. Nothing is dropped silently: every node is in exactly one place, a text unit's or a table's `node_ids`, a picture's own image node, a form field's own node, or `omitted`. It began as the view ParseBench's adapter (`ethos_bench.py` `_layout`) built and departs from it in four places, each a consumer's need: a DOCX paragraph is one element where the adapter had one per run; the label tier (level 7) is `text`, as both projections write it, where the adapter said heading; a role path is read after the RoleMap, as Markdown reads it, where the adapter read the raw path; and a table with no box is one `table` element without `bbox`, where the adapter dropped it and kept its runs as one element each. A form field is a `form-field` element of its own, with no `bbox` (decision #163). No verdict, no score: every label is one a record field states, every box one the record measured or the union of such boxes, every node id a copy.

parser_version.description: The engine build that projected this.

profile_sha256.description: The RECORD's own profile, copied from the representation's identity: the profile it was read under (a DOCX, XLSX or OCR record has its own). It names the reader rules the grouping and labels follow — reading order, layout units, furniture, headings, figures — so a change to one of them moves it. It does not cover `elements_rule`, which travels below instead, so adding this view moved no other artifact's digest.

source_sha256.description: Digest of the original source bytes, carried through from the representation.

representation_sha256.description: Digest of the representation the elements were built from: the binding that makes every `node_ids` entry resolvable. It does NOT cover geometry, which sits outside the representation's fingerprint by design (docs/01-CONTRACT.md §4), so it binds no `bbox` here.

elements_rule.description: This projection's own rule: how it groups, labels and orders. A change to any of those is a new id, never a flag on this one; a change to a reader rule it reads moves `profile_sha256` instead.

coordinate_system.description: The representation's own: integer centipoints, origin at the page's top-left, y growing down. Every `bbox` here is in it, in the frame of the page's media box (`width` × `height`).

pages.description: The pages the representation declares, in its order. Empty for a source with no pages (office formats), whose elements carry no `page` and no `bbox`.

index.description: The page's 1-based position in the document, in the page tree's order — physical, not a printed page label (`/PageLabels`). What an element's `page` names.

width.description: Page width in integer centipoints, after rotation.

height.description: Page height in integer centipoints, after rotation.

turn.description: Decision #155. Quarter turns clockwise beyond the declared rotation in which the page was read, its text drawn turned: the frame width, height and every `bbox` are in. Absent where 0.

visible.description: The box a viewer shows (decision #62), where it is narrower than the page. In the page's frame, turned by `turn` where the page was read turned (decision #155). A consumer drawing the page shows this box alone and places every `bbox` on its picture by it, turned back where `turn` says. Absent where the page shows the whole of its media box.

elements.description: Every element, in page order, and on a page in the representation's reading order: each sits at the first node it covers, and one covering none comes last on its page. Elements may overlap in one place only: a picture's `node_ids` and text repeat runs that are elements of their own.

omitted.description: What no element carries, one entry per reason that occurred, in the order the enum lists them; empty when nothing was left out. The nodes stay in the representation. `ethos-parser elements` also writes one line on stderr naming each reason and its count whenever this is not empty.

reason.description: `no-measured-box`: text runs on a page none of whose block has a measured box, as `ground` omits them. `whitespace-only`: a DOCX paragraph holding nothing but whitespace. `annotation`: an annotation's text, markup over the page. `image-not-painted`: an image whose placement is not an axis-aligned rectangle the record states. `figure-not-measured`: a figure region with no measured box; a region is no node, so `count` counts regions and `node_ids` is empty.

count.description: How many: nodes, or figure regions for `figure-not-measured`.

id.description: `e1`, `e2`, … in this artifact's order. Stable for one representation and one rule; not a representation node id.

label.description: The first label the record states. `page-header` and `page-footer`: a run's page `furniture` (decision #41), a Word header's or footer's (decision #136) included, read before anything else, so a running head the heading rule also read stays the page's header. `section-header`: a heading level 1-6 a DOCX paragraph, an ODF heading or an EPUB `h1`–`h6` declares, as both projections read it; a tagged `H` or `H1`–`H6` innermost on a run's role path after the document's `/RoleMap` (`standard_role_path`, as Markdown reads it); or a run the reader inferred a heading from its type at levels 1-6 (decision #29). The label tier, level 7 — a bold line at the head of its text (decision #47) — is `text`, as both projections write it. A role path whose innermost known role is `Caption` makes a `caption`, `LI`, `Lbl` or `LBody` a `list-item`, and `Title` settles it as `text` (decision #166); a DOCX paragraph's declared numbering is a `list-item` too. Every one is a role the document declares: none is read from a font size, a prefix or a bullet (docs/06-STEAL-REFUSE.md P14). A tagged `Table` role labels nothing. `table`: a table record. `picture`: a painted image placement or a figure region (decision #46). `form-field`: an interactive form field node (decision #163). `text`: anything else.

page.description: The `index` of its page: its 1-based position in the document. Absent for a source with no pages.

bbox.description: `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` in `coordinate_system`. A text unit's is the union of its runs' measured boxes; a table's and a cell's the record's measured box; a painted image's the rectangle its placement painted; a figure's its measured region. On a page every element has one except a table whose record has none (a tagged table's grid) and a form field, whose declared rectangle is not a measured box (decision #163); a source with no pages has none at all.

text.description: A text unit's blocks joined by one space, and a DOCX paragraph's runs as both projections write them, its tabs and line breaks kept; a table's cell texts joined by one space; a picture's text is that of each unit holding a run the record names inside it, joined by one space (decision #97), and may be empty; a form field's is its node's text, its value as text, which every widget of a radio group shares (`form_field.state` says which one is on).

node_ids.description: The representation nodes it covers, copied from the record: a text unit's runs in reading order, a run with no box of its own included; a table's cells' nodes, cell by cell; a painted image's own node, then the runs the record names inside it; a figure region's runs inside; a form field's own node. How a consumer binds an element back to the record: each id is a node of the representation named by `representation_sha256`.

level.description: A `section-header`'s level: the one a DOCX, ODF or EPUB file declares, the tagged `H1`–`H6` (`H` is 1), or the reader's inferred level, 1 where it states none. Absent on every other label.

table.description: The table record's grid. Present on every `table` element, and only there.

form_field.description: A form field's facts, copied from its node (decisions #162, #163). Present on every `form-field` element, and only there.

name.description: The fully qualified field name. Absent where the document names none.

label.description: The name the form gives the field for a person to read (decision #162). Absent where the field states none.

field_type.description: The field's type as the document spells it. Absent where no ancestor declares one.

value.description: The field's value, in the shape the document wrote it.

state.description: A check box's or radio button's state as its widget states it, or why it cannot be told (decision #162). Present on those two kinds of field only.

id.description: The table record's id in the representation.

detection_rule.description: Decision #165: the rule that produced the record, as it states it — a drawn grid, aligned whitespace, the document's own tags, a chart's printed values (`bar-labels-*`, `point-labels-*`, `slice-labels-*`: a table read from a chart, not a data table the page drew), or an office file's own. A table going on into later pages (decision #142) carries its first page's; the records named in `continued` keep their own rule, which may be another page rule (a drawn grid going on as aligned whitespace), never a tagged, chart or office one.

name.description: A worksheet's name, as its cells' locators state it (decision #135). Absent on any other table.

continued.description: The table records on the following pages this table goes on in (decision #142), in page order: their rows follow its own and their cells carry their page. Absent where it goes on in none.

headers_unbound.description: Decision #167: present, and true, where this table's header cells are named on none of its cells because binding them would pass the view's budget — sixteen steps a cell and a thousand more, a step being a row a cell covers, a header list it searches or an id it names (an id longer than 24 bytes a step for each 24). Only a crafted grid reaches it. The cells' own `header` flags stand. Absent on every other table.

cells.description: The record's cells, in its order, then those of each record in `continued`, its rows below this one's. A merged cell is one entry at its top-left slot.

rowspan.description: Rows it spans; 1 means not merged.

colspan.description: Columns it spans; 1 means not merged.

page.description: Its page's `index`, where that is not its element's: a cell of a table going on from the page before (decision #142). Absent on every other cell.

bbox.description: The cell's measured box. Absent where the record has none.

text.description: The cell's text, as the record holds it.

node_ids.description: The nodes the record places in this cell.

id.description: Decision #167: the cell record's id, which the header lists name.

header.description: Decision #167: the record states this is a header cell. Omitted when false.

column_headers.description: Decision #167: on a cell that is no header, the column headers over it, top first, by id: the non-empty cells of the nearest run of all-header rows above it whose columns meet its own, so a header a table repeats part way down heads only the rows under it. Omitted when empty.

row_headers.description: Decision #167: on a cell that is no header, the row headers before it, left first, by id: the non-empty header cells outside an all-header row whose rows meet its own. Omitted when empty.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The first line of body text runs on to a second line and a third and a fourth before a fifth line closes the paragraph
